claim_updates.reason: MEASUREMENT_INVALID per frozen decision_rule: C7 fails (0/3 sites with >=50 non-leakage transitions; Wikipedia 8, GitHub 4, MDN 2). This is an infrastructure/data-sufficiency failure, not a scientific negative. Structural URL-level leakage (78-92% of link navigations have action.target_href == state_after.url) on server-rendered MPAs (Wikipedia/MDN/GitHub) makes the NL filter remove most transitions by design of these sites. After filtering, Wikipedia's 8 NL transitions have 6 unique SA pairs (all singleton), so Laplace-smoothed BC PMI = 0.0 bits is mathematically forced (I(X;Y)=0 when each (s,a) appears once). Positive control passes strongly (BC PMI = 1.841, p=0.001) validating the estimator on deterministic in-memory data. No evidence accumulated for or against C-WEB-DYNAMICS from this experiment. Claim ceiling bounded to: server-rendered MPAs with link-dominated Playwright navigation and exact href==URL leakage definition cannot express the tested effect at transition-level PMI with 50 NL threshold.

next_question: Should the Physics lane pivot to production SPAs with hash-based client-side routing (e.g., TodoMVC hash-SPA variants, React Router history-based SPAs) where multiple client-side states can share the same URL path, reducing URL-level leakage below 40% and enabling >=50 non-leakage transitions for PMI analysis?
reason: Frozen decision_rule triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID on C7 (data sufficiency): 0/3 production server-rendered sites yield >=50 non-leakage transitions. The structural blocker is 78-92% URL-level leakage on Wikipedia/MDN/GitHub where <a href> encodes the full destination URL, making action.target_href == state_after.url by construction for link-based navigation. This is not a measurement artifact but a fundamental property of server-rendered MPAs: links are designed to navigate to their encoded destination. Even with unlimited collection time, 50 NL transitions at 92% leakage (MDN) would require ~625 raw transitions. The audit correctly identifies site selection as the root cause: production SPAs with hash/history client-side routing, form submissions, and button clicks should exhibit lower leakage. The PMI pipeline itself is validated by the positive control (BC 1.841, p=0.001). The next experiment must address the synthetic-to-real gap by testing on genuine SPAs rather than server-rendered MPAs.
